title: Bulletproof Vest Partnership Grant Program Reauthorization Act of 2015
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the Senate on May 6, 2015. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Bulletproof Vest Partnership Grant Program Reauthorization Act of 2015

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to extend through FY2020 the authorization of appropriations for the Bulletproof Vest Partnership (BVP) program.

(Sec. 3) It requires the transfer to the general fund of the Treasury, no later than January 31, 2023, of all funds appropriated for the BVP program for FY2016-FY2020 that are not obligated on or before December 31, 2022.

(Sec. 4) The bill expresses the sense of Congress that amounts made available to carry out the BVP program should be made available through the end of the fiscal year following the one for which the amounts are appropriated and should not be made available until expended.

(Sec. 5) It prohibits the use of federal funds under another grant program to pay or defer the cost of the matching funds requirement for the BVP program.

(Sec. 6) It requires a state, local, or tribal government that receives a BVP program grant to comply with BVP program requirements, to have a written policy requiring uniformed patrol officers to wear an armor vest or body armor, and to use the funds to purchase vests or body armor that meet performance standards established by the Bureau of Justice Assistance.

(Sec. 7) The bill allows preferential consideration to a BVP program grant applicant from a jurisdiction that provides armor vests that are uniquely fitted to law enforcement officers, including individual female officers.

summary.headline: This law extends a federal grant program that helps state, local, and tribal governments buy bulletproof vests for police and other officers.
summary.what_it_does: It extends the Bulletproof Vest Partnership program's funding authorization through fiscal year 2020 and sets a deadline for returning unused program money to the general fund of the Treasury. It bars using other federal grant money to cover the local matching share required for these vest grants. Grant recipients must have a written policy requiring uniformed patrol officers to wear vests and must buy vests that meet standards set by the Bureau of Justice Assistance. Applicants whose jurisdictions provide vests fitted for individual officers, including female officers, may get preferred consideration.

who_it_affects.group: State, local, and tribal law enforcement agencies
who_it_affects.how: They can keep applying for federal matching funds to buy armor vests through 2020, but must adopt a written vest-wearing policy and buy vests that meet federal performance standards.
Grant-receiving agencies must require them to wear armor vests or body armor under their written policies.
Applicants whose jurisdictions provide vests uniquely fitted to individual officers, including women, may receive preferred consideration for grants.

who_it_affects.group: Local governments that rely on federal grant money to meet matching requirements
who_it_affects.how: They cannot use other federal grant funds to pay or defer their share of the vest program's matching costs.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 16, 2016; the funding extension covers fiscal years 2016 through 2020, and unobligated funds must be transferred to the Treasury by January 31, 2023.
